core.text: Observed: one 300 rpm run stopped at second 60 and yielded approximately 2.4 percent final-vial spread. This bounded counterexample challenges universal necessity of sustained 900 rpm and optical stability. The fluctuating 900 rpm images lack matched final samples, so they establish neither gradients nor a disturbance feedback mechanism.

Proposed six-trial session: two fresh fixed-duration 300/900 rpm pairs, reversing speed order in the second pair; run each for 60 seconds and sample at second 120. Then compare fresh 900 rpm timer-stop and enabled-rule trials, both capped at second 105. Fix recipe, addition location, bottle and camera; alternate sampling order. Log images every five seconds, cessation times, depression, specks, raw vials and duration. Use references and spill tray; stop on escaped liquid.

Retain both accounts until separating observations arrive. In fixed trials, record shadow-rule failures without restarting. Only the final-vial proxy determines target success; report all failures. Repeated lower-speed success would support dispensability in these conditions. Enabled-rule success after timer-stop failure would favor useful additional agitation, without establishing necessity of this speed or stop rule.

residue.text: Specks remain unidentified: bubbles, reflections and undissolved dye remain possibilities. Available surface and frame observations cannot measure bubble fraction or establish the proposed optical-to-agitation return loop.

Common-aliquot repeatability is not concentration calibration; commanded rpm lacks independent verification. Sampling may disturb gradients. Enabled and timer-stopped trials have different quiet durations before second 120, limiting attribution to extra stirring. A rapid image change after stopping could reflect surface shape or settling.

Six trials permit little replication. One observed lower-speed success does not establish reliable sufficiency; proposed successes remain hypotheses. Other viscosities, solutes, vessels and continuous processes are untested.

tension.account_a: Hypothesis: failed 900 rpm optical checks primarily reflect agitation-renewed disturbances after the final-vial outcome is already achievable; continued feedback-driven agitation is unnecessary in the tested recipe.
tension.account_b: Incompatible rival hypothesis: failed checks primarily reflect unresolved depth gradients; continued agitation is required for the tested final-vial outcome.
tension.prediction_a: With fixed 60-second runs, 900 rpm images would fluctuate more and spread would fall promptly after stopping while final vials meet the target. In the feedback comparison, both runs would pass despite shadow failures, with the timer run using less stirring if the enabled rule prolongs operation.
tension.prediction_b: Fixed 60-second runs would retain final-vial spread above 4 percent; in the feedback comparison, the longer enabled run would pass while the timer run fails. Persistent side spread with passing final vials, both failures, or overlapping results would leave these accounts unresolved.
